summary_html: A **court reverses or vacates** a CPS or agency decision due to procedural error, insufficient evidence, or constitutional violation. Federal review data (CFSR, ASFA) tracks judicial determinations on reasonable efforts and due process.
authority_html:
- **Adoption and Safe Families Act (ASFA)** — judicial findings of 'reasonable efforts' compliance  
- **CFSR Regulations (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal review of judicial/agency conformity  
- **42 U.S.C. § 1983** — civil-rights remedy for unconstitutional removals (14th & 4th Amendments).

key_cases.case_name: Lyon v. Department of Children & Family Services
key_cases.holding: The court held that DCFS violated Lyon's due process rights by combining the low credible-evidence standard for indicating a report and deciding the first-stage appeal with delays beyond its own regulatory deadlines, and affirmed expungement from the State Central Register.
key_cases.relevance: A court will set aside an indicated finding when DCFS misses the deadlines its own rules impose.
key_cases.quote: we require strict statutory and regulatory compliance only if the Department uses the credible-evidence standard to indicate a report and to consider a first-stage appeal

key_cases.holding: The court held that the circuit court could not disregard a DCFS administrative abuse finding by conducting its own de novo review, reversed the change of custody as against the manifest weight of the evidence, and reinstated DCFS as guardian with power to consent to adoption.
key_cases.relevance: Shows the limits on a circuit court's power to reverse an agency's abuse finding.
key_cases.quote: The court, without authority, rejected an administrative finding that the Wards abused Austin after conducting a de novo review of the matter.

key_cases.case_name: Burris v. Department of Children & Family Services
key_cases.holding: The court reversed, holding that once a court has entered a judicial finding of child neglect on the same issue, section 7.16 of the Reporting Act and DCFS Rule 336.190(a)(3) require dismissal of an administrative appeal seeking expungement of the indicated report.
key_cases.relevance: Defines when a reviewing court will and will not reopen an agency's substantiated finding.
key_cases.quote: plaintiff's administrative appeal requesting expungement of the report of child neglect should have been dismissed pursuant to section 7.16 of the Reporting Act

key_cases.holding: The court reversed an order closing the case to private guardianship with the paternal grandmother, holding the best-interests finding was against the manifest weight of the evidence where the mother had complied with services and every caseworker recommended return home.
key_cases.relevance: A recent reversal of a permanency decision that ran against the agency's own recommendations.
key_cases.quote: The circuit court's finding that this was in K.W.'s best interest was against the manifest weight of the evidence.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the neglect adjudication and wardship of a newborn, holding Illinois had jurisdiction under the UCCJEA even though the child was delivered in Indiana, that the ex parte shelter-care notice complaint was moot, and that the injurious-environment finding was not against the manifest weight of the evidence.
key_cases.relevance: Supplies the manifest-weight standard of review that governs every appellate challenge to an Illinois neglect adjudication.
key_cases.quote: On review, a trial court's ruling of neglect will not be reversed unless it is against the manifest weight of the evidence.

timeline_requirements.requirement_name: Request to amend or expunge an indicated report
timeline_requirements.deadline: 60 days, tolled until any related criminal or juvenile court action concludes (325 ILCS 5/7.16)

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Loss of the departmental hearing to amend or remove the report from the State Central Register (325 ILCS 5/7.16)
